title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.16-18): Grothendieck works with the moduli space MB~_{g,nu} of compact oriented hyperbolic (conformal) surfaces with 'generalized boundary'. Each of the nu holes is either a geodesic circle of length l_i>0 or a cusp (l_i=0). Rigidified by a reference surface X_0, this space is homeomorphic to C^d x (R^+)^nu. It contains the Teichmueller space M~_{g,nu} of nu-punctured surfaces as the stratum where all l_i=0. He wants an intrinsic retraction MB~ -> M~, independent of any pants decomposition.

The construction carried over from p.16 is conformal filling. Each geodesic boundary circle is a Riemannian oriented circle. Glue in the flat cone on it; the cone's conformal structure is canonical. The result is a closed Riemann surface X^ with nu marked points s_i (the cone apices, or the cusps for degenerate holes). Passing to isomorphism classes gives the desired retraction.

This page observes that X^ carries more data: mutually disjoint closed discs D_i around the s_i (the glued cones), with D_i = {s_i} for cusps. A disc system on (X^, s_i) is called 'admissible' if it arises this way. He gives an intrinsic criterion. Each boundary circle Gamma_i = dD_i carries two U(1)-actions:
(1) Rotations of D_i. Uniformize (D_i, s_i) to (unit disc, 0); the resulting rotation action on the boundary is independent of choices.
(2) Normalized arc length along Gamma_i, for the unique complete hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary on X^ \ union of the open D_j (cusps at degenerate centres).
Admissibility means these two actions coincide. Equivalently, harmonic measure on Gamma_i seen from s_i in D_i is proportional to hyperbolic length on the complement.

For fixed (X^, s_i) he counts nu parameters, matching the dimension count: real dim MB = 6g-6+3nu, so the fibres over M have dimension nu. He proposes to read these parameters as radii. A conformal disc D with interior point s embeds canonically in T_sD as the unit disc: take the Riemann map f with f(s)=0 and use (df_s)^{-1} o f, which is rotation-independent. This is the conformal-radius construction. So each D_i gives a round disc Delta_i in T_{s_i}, i.e. a hermitian norm |z| <= r_i on T_{s_i}, well defined up to scale. The non-degenerate radii at s_i form an R^{+*}-torsor R_i, the positive half of the real line |T_{s_i}|; adding radius 0 gives an R^+-torsor-like closure.

The next page states the conjecture this serves: the radii determine the admissible system, and the realizable radii form a product region r_i < rho_i. He notes a mismatch with the expected (R^+)^I-action unless rho_i = infinity, and reduces everything to admissible triples of discs on the Riemann sphere around 0, 1, infinity (the 'orange slices' model).
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The admissibility criterion is correct as a characterization. The flat cone over a circle of length l is rotationally symmetric, so its conformal boundary parametrization is proportional to arc length. Conversely, matching parametrizations allow regluing the flat cone conformally.

Implicit assumptions are left unstated. The complement X^ minus the open discs must be given its unique hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary (cusps at degenerate centres). The boundary curves must be regular enough (real-analytic) for the gluing to define a conformal structure.
The claim that the discs Delta_i in T_{s_i} are 'discs in the strict euclidean sense' is automatic: they are images of the unit disc under a C-linear map, hence round for the conformal norm.

The claim that admissible systems on fixed (X^, s_i) depend on exactly nu parameters is only a dimension count, not proved. The next page admits a tension between the radii picture and the hoped-for (R^+)^I-action.
Minor language slips: 'unequality' (Gallicism for inequality), 'module 1' (for modulus 1).

ideas.what: Moduli of hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of lengths l_i >= 0, with punctured moduli as the stratum l=0, and the search for an intrinsic retraction onto it.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli space M_{g,n}(L) of bordered hyperbolic surfaces / its bordification by cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates; studied systematically by Mirzakhani (2007), Mondello (2009-11), Do-Norbury
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on the Teichmueller tower and pants decompositions, discusses holes versus punctures in M_{g,nu}; the specific bordered space and retraction are not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Retraction of bordered moduli onto punctured moduli by gluing flat cones on the boundary geodesics (conformal filling).
ideas.modern_name: Conformal filling / capping of geodesic boundary by flat cones
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related cone-surface constructions in Do-Norbury and Tan-Wong-Zhang (cone angles as imaginary lengths)

ideas.what: Intrinsic criterion for 'admissible' disc systems: the rotation U(1)-action on each disc boundary must coincide with the arc-length U(1)-action of the hyperbolic complement with geodesic boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Matching of harmonic measure with hyperbolic boundary length; circle actions on boundary components
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standardly formulated. The boundary U(1)-bundles appear in Mirzakhani's symplectic-reduction proof of Witten's conjecture (2007)

ideas.what: A disc around s embeds canonically in T_s as a unit disc, so each disc gives a norm on T_s (its radius). Radii at s_i form an R^{+*}-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Conformal (mapping) radius; norm on the tangent line, i.e. a point of the R^+-torsor attached to L_i^dual where c_1(L_i)=psi_i
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (conformal radius); in moduli theory, decorations by horocycles or tangent norms in Penner (1987) and related work

ideas.what: Conjecture: on fixed (X^, s_i), admissible disc systems are parametrized by their radii, filling a product region r_i < rho_i (continued next page).
ideas.modern_name: Coordinatization of fibres of the filling map M_{g,n}(L) -> M_{g,n} by conformal radii of the capping discs
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; not aware of a standard result

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes the 'conformal filling' map from bordered hyperbolic surfaces to punctured Riemann surfaces with admissible disc systems. He conjectures that the conformal radii in the tangent spaces T_{s_i} coordinatize the nu-dimensional fibres, giving a canonical description of the bordification by cusps (and on the next page reduces this to admissible disc triples on P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}). I know of no published treatment of exactly this filling map and its radius coordinates.
missed.quote: the possible admissible systems of discs around the points s_i depend on nu parameters - and the first idea which flips to mind ... is to view them as being the "radii" of those discs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such a description would give a pants-decomposition-free fibration of M_{g,n}(L) over M_{g,n}. Its fibre coordinates live naturally in the norm torsors of the cotangent lines whose Chern classes are the psi_i. This could give a conformal-geometric counterpart to Mirzakhani's symplectic reduction (l^2/2 vs psi_i) and to Penner-style decorations.

missed.claim: The admissibility condition is phrased as coincidence of two circle actions on each boundary component. The radius parameters are points of the R^+-torsor of norms on T_{s_i}. Together these tie the boundary U(1)-bundles of bordered moduli to the tautological tangent lines at the punctures. This is the same pairing that later underlies the psi-class / boundary-length relation in Mirzakhani's volume recursion, here seen conformally rather than symplectically.
missed.quote: the two operations we got of the standard circle group ... upon Gamma_i ... should be the same
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests an explicit conformal model for the degeneration l_i -> 0 in which the U(1)-bundle over M_{g,n}(L) is identified with the unit circle bundle of T_{s_i} via conformal radius. This might give direct geometric proofs of known asymptotics as l -> 0.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clean, intrinsic and correct formulation of admissible capping discs via matching circle actions, and the conformal-radius parametrization by tangent-space torsors. It anticipates themes later developed by Penner, Mirzakhani and Mondello in different language. The specific filling-plus-radii construction does not seem to be in the literature. However, the content is exploratory and largely a reformulation rather than a finished result, so a specialist would find it interesting but not startling.

'by stating that [-the-] for every' - the struck word is typed over ('thx'/'the'); the reading is fine.
'an [-arbitrary-] admissible system' - the struck word appears as typed-over 'anxxxx'; the intended reading 'an admissible system' is correct.
'this metric being [-defined-] {+unique+} up to a scalar factor' - correct; 'unique' is handwritten above.
'The set {+R_i+} of all those possible discs (the non-degenerate ones, say)' - the typed text reads 'one$ say', which should be 'ones, say'.
'unequality' is in the original (Grothendieck's Gallicism), not a transcription error.
